original_question: Let f: Ω → X be a function on a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) with values in a Banach space X. If T_1 and T_2 are two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon, and f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T_2?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.8 (Fremlin) in Section 3.3 (“McShane integral”), on whether generalized McShane integrability depends on the choice of quasi-Radon topology on the same complete probability space. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct official target almost verbatim: the same objects f:Ω→X, the same complete probability space (Ω,Σ,μ), the same pair of topologies T1,T2 on Ω, the same hypothesis that f is McShane integrable with respect to T1, and the same question of whether integrability must then hold with respect to T2. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient conventions are implicit: all topological spaces are Hausdorff and all Banach spaces are real. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, “μ is quasi-Radon for T_i” should be unpacked as: T_i⊂Σ and (Ω,T_i,Σ,μ) is a quasi-Radon probability space, meaning that μ is inner regular with respect to the T_i-closed sets and μ(⋃𝒢)=sup{μ(G):G∈𝒢} for every upwards directed family 𝒢⊂T_i. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

The problem concerns the generalized McShane integral for functions on quasi-Radon probability spaces, not just the classical [0,1]-version stated earlier in the subsection. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

It helps to make explicit that the same underlying measurable probability space (Ω,Σ,μ) is being endowed with each of the two topologies, and the question is whether McShane integrability is independent of that topological choice. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a real Banach space, let (Ω,Σ,μ) be a complete probability space, and let T1 and T2 be Hausdorff topologies on Ω such that, for each i∈{1,2}, T_i⊂Σ and (Ω,T_i,Σ,μ) is a quasi-Radon probability space; that is, μ is inner regular with respect to the T_i-closed sets and μ(⋃𝒢)=sup{μ(G):G∈𝒢} for every upwards directed family 𝒢⊂T_i. If f:Ω→X is McShane integrable with respect to T1 in the generalized quasi-Radon sense, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T2? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1607.07787 is exactly Problem 3.8 in Section 3.3, so your draft is already very close. I only made explicit the hidden conventions and the definition of quasi-Radon that the paper gives immediately beforehand, and clarified that the intended notion is the generalized McShane integral on quasi-Radon probability spaces. I did not broaden the question beyond the survey’s probability-space formulation. The paper also records the known positive case that the answer is affirmative when T1 has a countable basis. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
